2.  Board of Library Trustees Temporary Ad Hoc Committee
  Recommendation:
  Receive a report on the Board of Library Trustees Temporary Ad Hoc Committee
  and provide direction to staff regarding its composition and duration.

  Deputy City Administrator Hernandez provided a brief presentation on Item No. 2
  and requested direction from the Board on the composition and duration of the
  committee. She informed the City Council that Trustee Ybarra was currently the
  only member on the committee after the recent retirement of former Mayor Lopez.

  President Ybarra inquired about the possibility of having residents serve on the
  committee as opposed to it only being comprised of sitting board members. City
  Attorney Moussa-Milward informed the Board that they have the discretion to
  appoint anyone to serve and reminded them of the narrow scope and temporary
  nature of an ad hoc committee. President Ybarra expressed her preference to see
  the committee grow and to include input from the community by having a resident
  serve on the committee.

  President Ybarra asked that staff come back with a recommendation on potential
  programs to allow the committee to concur and confer on ideas to promote literacy
  in the community.

  Trustee Larios volunteered to serve on the ad hoc committee along with an
  appointment of a resident. There was a consensus from the Library Board to have
  Trustee Larios serve and consider expanding the committee to include residents.

  City Administrator Saeki commented that a subsequent item would be brought
  back to the Board to clarify the scope of the ad hoc committee, discuss expanding
  the committee, and outline the process for appointing a community member.

   Board of Library Trustees Agenda Report

Meeting Date:  August 18, 2026
From:  Brian Saeki, City Administrator
Department:  City Administration
Submitted by:  Diana Figueroa, Communications and Public Information Manager

Subject
Board of Library Trustees Temporary Ad Hoc Committee

Recommendation
A. Provide direction to staff on the possible recruitment for Vernon resident participants for the
Board of Library Trustees (Board) Temporary Ad Hoc Committee with the understanding that
inclusion of a non-Board member would subject the committee to Brown Act notice and agenda
requirements pursuant to California Government Code section 54952(b); and
B. Determine the specific objective of the Board’s Temporary Ad Hoc Committee and its date of
dissolution.

Background
Section 2.24.050 of the Vernon Municipal Code (VMC) authorizes the Board of Library Trustees
to make and enforce all rules, regulations, and bylaws necessary for the administration of the
library, prescribe duties and powers of the librarian, purchase books, and purchase property or
equip buildings for such libraries.

At its June 2, 2020 meeting, the Board established a Library Temporary Ad Hoc Committee (Ad
Hoc Committee), of no more than two Trustees, to work with staff to determine a plan to
reestablish the Vernon Public Library. On June 7, 2022, the Board appointed Trustee Melissa
Ybarra to serve on the Ad Hoc Committee along with, now retired, Trustee Leticia Lopez. With
the retirement of Trustee Lopez, staff sought direction from the Board at its July 7, 2026 Special
Meeting, regarding its desire to continue with the Ad Hoc Committee.

Staff received direction to include Board President Ybarra and Trustee Larios on the Ad Hoc
Committee along with Vernon resident(s). It should be noted that, pursuant to California
Government Code section 54952(b), inclusion of a resident or other non-member of the Board
would change the Ad Hoc Committee from a non-Brown Act body to a legislative body subject to
Brown Act requirements. To proceed with the formation of the Ad Hoc Committee, staff are now
seeking guidance from the Board on the possible recruitment of residents, the targeted objective
of the Ad Hoc Committee, and the committee’s duration.

If City Council wishes to facilitate resident member recruitment for the Ad Hoc Committee, some
details that staff recommend the Board consider are:
  • Target number of residents to serve on Ad Hoc Committee
  • Duration of community outreach/recruitment efforts to assess interest
  • Member selection criteria

To determine a specific goal for the Ad Hoc Committee (which will likely influence the Ad Hoc
Committee’s timeline), the Board may wish to consider exploring the following topics:
  • Little Free Library Project
  • Vernon Reads! Programs
  • Library-related grant opportunities and funding

  Item 2  Page 7 of 8
   •  Literacy initiatives
  •  New child, teen, and/or adult programming
  •  Partnerships with local organizations

With definitive direction from the Board regarding its vision for the Ad Hoc Committee, including
its specific task and timeline for completion, staff will be better able to assist the Ad Hoc
Committee with planning and coordination.
